issues.legal_issue: A conviction for abetting forgery and cheating may stand where an accused identified an impostor as a genuine executant and the claimed honest mistake was unsupported by evidence.
material_facts: The accused, a village Lambardar, identified a woman who was impersonating the actual co-owner as that co-owner during execution and registration of a mortgage deed.
The Sub-Registrar would not have registered the deed but for the accused’s identification.
The accused was expected to know the actual co-owner, and the evidence did not support his claim that he innocently believed the impersonator was her.
The trial court convicted the accused, the High Court affirmed the conviction while reducing the sentence, and the Supreme Court considered his appeal.
issues.conclusion: The Court found no ground to interfere with the concurrent findings, affirmed the conviction, and dismissed the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 34(3) and 35(1) of the Registration Act, the registering officer must inquire whether a document was executed by the persons said to have executed it and satisfy himself as to the identity of those appearing. The accused’s identification enabled registration; his position and expected knowledge of the true executant, together with the absence of evidence supporting his asserted innocent mistake, supported the conviction under Sections 467 and 417 read with Section 109 of the Indian Penal Code. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and accused_identified_impostor_as_genuine_executant and identification_enabled_registration and accused_expected_to_know_true_executant and no_evidence_supports_innocent_mistake

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The accused appealed against a criminal conviction.
predicates.accused_identified_impostor_as_genuine_e: The accused identified a person impersonating the true executant as that genuine executant.
predicates.identification_enabled_registration: The registering officer would not have registered the document without the accused’s identification.
predicates.accused_expected_to_know_true_executant: The accused’s role or circumstances gave reason to expect that he knew the true executant.
predicates.no_evidence_supports_innocent_mistake: The evidence did not support the accused’s claim that he innocently mistook the impostor for the true executant.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals a conviction after identifying an impostor as a genuine executant, and that identification enabled registration, the accused was expected to know the true executant, and no evidence supports an innocent mistake, the conviction is affirmed and the appeal is dismissed.
